bull.b: The reported cash position and planned cost reductions provide substantial operating runway through Q4 2028, giving Quantum-Si time to complete Proteus development and pursue commercialization without immediate financing pressure. This supports strategic continuity over the next several quarters.

Progress toward broad amino-acid coverage strengthens the technical case for Proteus and could improve its usefulness across demanding proteomics workflows. Advancing from development results toward routine sequencing capability supports differentiation if the platform achieves reliable commercial performance.

A qualified interest base across academic, institutional, and biopharmaceutical users indicates that Quantum-Si has identified concrete applications for Proteus rather than relying only on a broad market narrative. This provides a foundation for adoption once access and deployment begin.

bear.b: The steep revenue decline shows that current commercial activity remains small and vulnerable to delayed capital purchases and customer timing. Persistently low sales reduce operating leverage, limit internally generated funding, and make successful Proteus commercialization increasingly important to the growth profile.

Large recurring losses relative to revenue indicate that the existing business model has not yet reached scale economics. Continued negative EBITDA and cash consumption can erode shareholder capital over time, even with a substantial cash balance, and leave future progress dependent on execution and funding discipline.

The delayed launch pushes customer access and potential revenue contribution further out, extending the period in which Quantum-Si must fund development without meaningful product scale. Repeatability and manufacturing challenges also create execution risk around commercial readiness, yields, and customer confidence.
